answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation costly to fake: each agent's work history forms a single verifiable thread of signed tasks, and rewards flow only along threads that survived real scrutiny. When a tide of fresh identities floods in, they start with no thread and earn trust slowly, while long-lived agents keep an ivory-standard record that is expensive to imitate. Duplicating that history across many fake agents costs more than it pays, so sybils stay shallow and untrusted.
